sections.name: architecture
sections.value: Doctrine: .agents/skills/pij-team/TENETS.md. u1 (shell + Rust installer): the statusline script is POSIX sh reading Claude's JSON on stdin (see the operator's current ~/.claude/statusline-context.sh for the segments to preserve). Resolve rs by pane: `pij-rs` has whoami/state — check `pij-rs whoami --help`; if it needs a seat, use `pij-rs list` filtered by pane (still ms) or POST /v1/whoami with {"TMUX_PANE":...} and the daemon.key bearer (see crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs caller struct). Colour: ANSI yellow `\033[33m` for rs, dim `\033[2m` for legacy; Claude statusline renders ANSI. Installer: extend crates/harnesses/src/claude_settings.rs (plans 126/127 — merged/merging: rebase onto origin/main after #349) with ensure_claude_statusline(homes, script) using the same backup/additive/report discipline; doctor verb `doctor claude-statusline`. u2 (TS): core/session-name.ts publishSeatName gets a generation arg; index.ts passes "rs" on the RustRuntimeSession path and "legacy" on the FsRegistry path; name = `rs·<id>`; investigate whether omp's session_name segment renders ANSI (probably not) — if not, setStatus(PIJ_STATUS_KEY, `\x1b[33mrs\x1b[0m <id>`) as the coloured second surface. Fakes as in plans 125/127.

Default: each coder gets its own worktree, branching off the PM's plan branch; unit lands back onto the plan branch (PM merges — coders never merge). Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (staged sweeps, untrustworthy greens) — only choose it for trivially disjoint single-wave work, and then file-scoped `git add` only, never -A. REMEMBER: fences partition WRITE intent, not the build — a mid-refactor sibling can still break your compile, so waves must respect build dependencies, and a broken workspace build is a PM composition concern, not a coder's to fix cross-fence.
